identity.description: The Necrobinder is a dark summoner who fights alongside Osty, an undead companion. The Necrobinder manipulates death itself through Doom (instant kill thresholds), Souls (free cycling cards), and Osty (a companion that tanks and attacks). The Necrobinder's playstyle is uniquely strategic — managing Osty's HP as a secondary defensive resource while stacking Doom to execute enemies.
identity.playstyle: Companion-based strategy with death mechanics. The Necrobinder manages three unique resources: Osty (your living shield and attacker), Doom (a debuff that instantly kills enemies when their HP drops below the Doom threshold), and Souls (zero-cost draw-2 cards that exhaust after use). Mastering all three systems simultaneously is the key to Necrobinder success.
strengths: Osty acts as a second health pool — enemies targeting Osty are not damaging you
Doom bypasses the need to deal the last X damage to enemies — efficiency in combat
Souls provide free card cycling that naturally thins your deck during combat
Unique approach to damage — combining direct damage with Doom thresholds for efficient kills
Strong exhaust synergies through Souls and other exhaust-on-use effects
Osty can be resummoned — even when Osty dies, the Necrobinder can bring it back
weaknesses: Osty management adds complexity — mismanaging Osty can leave you vulnerable
Doom is a threshold check, not direct damage — enemies must also take regular damage
Souls exhaust after one use per combat — your free cycling is finite
Some enemies target you directly, bypassing Osty's tanking benefit
Requires understanding multiple unique systems simultaneously
Can struggle against enemies with very high HP that are hard to Doom efficiently

osty.description: Osty is automatically summoned at the start of every combat. Osty has its own HP pool, can take damage from enemies, and can be commanded to attack or use abilities through specific Necrobinder cards.
osty.hp_pool: Osty has a separate HP pool. Enemies may target Osty instead of you.
osty.auto_summon: Osty is summoned automatically at the start of each combat — no card or energy cost required.
osty.death_and_resummon: If Osty dies during combat, certain cards and effects can resummon it. Some strategies even benefit from Osty dying and being resummoned.

doom_system.description: Doom is a debuff applied to enemies. When an enemy's current HP is less than or equal to their Doom value at the end of their turn, they are instantly killed. This means you don't need to deal ALL the damage — just enough to push their HP below the Doom threshold.
how_to_use: Apply Doom to enemies through Necrobinder cards
Deal direct damage to reduce the enemy's HP toward the Doom threshold
Once enemy HP <= Doom, they die at the end of their turn
Doom + direct damage is more efficient than direct damage alone
Example: Enemy has 50 HP. Apply 20 Doom. You only need to deal 31 damage instead of 50.
doom_system.efficiency_calculation: Doom effectively reduces enemy HP for the purpose of killing them. 20 Doom on a 50 HP enemy means you only need 31 damage to trigger the kill. This saves 19 damage worth of effort.
doom_system.vs_high_hp_enemies: Against very high HP enemies, Doom requires significant investment. Sometimes direct damage is more efficient for enemies over 100 HP unless you can apply 40+ Doom.
doom_system.vs_multi_enemies: Spreading Doom across multiple enemies can be efficient in AOE encounters, but be careful not to spread too thin.

souls_system.description: Souls are unique zero-cost skill cards. When played, they draw 2 cards and then exhaust. They exist in your deck at the start of combat and provide free cycling that naturally thins your deck.
key_properties: 0 energy cost — completely free to play
Exhaust after being played — removed from combat deck
Reset between combats — full Souls back at start of each fight
Can be generated during combat through specific effects
strategic_use: Play Souls immediately for free cycling — there's almost never a reason to hold them
Souls thin your deck as they exhaust, improving future draw quality
Exhaust synergy cards trigger when Souls exhaust
In long fights, generating additional Souls extends your cycling advantage
Souls make your opening turns stronger — free draw 2 means seeing more of your deck immediately

osty_management.description: Managing Osty effectively is one of the most important skills for the Necrobinder. Osty serves as a tank, an attacker, and a strategic tool.
as_tank: Enemies that target Osty deal damage to Osty instead of you — free HP preservation
Monitor which enemies are targeting Osty vs targeting you each turn
Healing or buffing Osty's HP extends its tanking capability
A healthy Osty can absorb 2-3 turns of enemy attacks
as_attacker: Specific cards command Osty to attack — these attacks don't cost YOUR attack cards
Osty attacks can be enhanced through buffs and specific Necrobinder effects
Osty's damage output is supplementary — don't rely on it as your primary damage source
Some builds empower Osty's attacks significantly, making it a primary damage dealer
death_management: When Osty dies, you lose your tank — be prepared to block directly
Some cards benefit from Osty dying (death triggers, resummon effects)
Resummoning Osty mid-combat can reset its HP and provide a fresh tank
Don't panic when Osty dies — adapt your strategy to play more defensively until resummon

osty_builds.description: Focus on empowering Osty as both a powerful attacker and a durable tank. Buff Osty's damage and HP, and use Osty-centric cards to command it in combat.
core_strategy: Buff Osty's attack damage through Necrobinder-specific cards
Increase Osty's HP or provide Osty-specific block to extend its tanking
Use Osty attack commands frequently to generate free damage
Resummon cards provide backup if Osty falls
Balance Osty investment with personal defense
key_cards: Cards that command Osty to attack
Cards that buff Osty's stats (damage, HP)
Cards that heal or protect Osty
Cards that resummon Osty after death
Cards that trigger effects when Osty attacks or takes damage
strengths: Osty provides a second character's worth of attacks and HP
Enemy attacks on Osty are attacks not hitting you
Osty builds can have both strong offense AND defense through companion management
Resummon mechanics make Osty builds resilient — Osty can come back from death
weaknesses: Requires Osty-specific cards — generic Necrobinder cards may not synergize
If Osty dies and you can't resummon, you lose a significant portion of your strategy
Some enemies bypass or ignore Osty, targeting you directly
Investing heavily in Osty can leave your personal cards underdeveloped

doom_builds.description: Focus on applying massive Doom to enemies and combining it with direct damage to trigger instant kills efficiently. The Doom build is about efficiency — killing enemies with less total damage investment.
core_strategy: Stack Doom quickly through high-Doom-application cards
Combine Doom with direct damage to push enemies below the kill threshold
Calculate Doom efficiency: how much Doom vs how much direct damage is optimal
Use Doom for efficient elite kills — save damage for the kill threshold push
AOE Doom application can handle multi-enemy encounters efficiently
key_cards: Cards that apply large amounts of Doom
Cards that apply Doom AND deal damage simultaneously
Cards that scale Doom application over time
Cards that apply Doom to multiple enemies
Direct damage cards to complement Doom and push HP below threshold
strengths: Very efficient damage — Doom means you deal less total damage to kill enemies
Strong against moderate-HP enemies where Doom threshold is easily reached
Doom stacks persist — continued Doom application compounds over turns
Can handle both single-target and multi-target with appropriate Doom cards
weaknesses: Doom alone doesn't kill — you still need direct damage to push HP below Doom
Very high HP enemies (bosses) require enormous Doom investment
Doom check is at END of enemy turn — enemies get one more action before dying
Splitting focus between Doom and direct damage requires careful resource management

soul_builds.description: Focus on generating and using Souls for maximum cycling and exhaust synergy. Play many Souls per turn for free draw, then leverage exhaust triggers from their exhaust. Generate additional Souls during combat to sustain the engine.
core_strategy: Generate additional Souls during combat beyond starting Souls
Use exhaust triggers (cards that benefit when cards exhaust) with Souls
Cycle through your deck rapidly by playing Souls for free draw
Thin your deck aggressively through Soul exhausts for consistent draws
Pair with cards that benefit from high card throughput (many plays per turn)
key_cards: Cards that generate additional Souls during combat
Cards that trigger effects when cards are exhausted
Cards that benefit from drawing many cards per turn
Cards that benefit from playing many cards per turn
Direct damage and block cards to actually win while cycling
strengths: Massive card cycling — see your entire deck very quickly
Free card plays (0-cost Souls) enable playing many cards per turn
Exhaust synergies generate value from every Soul played
Extremely consistent once Soul generation is established
weaknesses: Souls are finite without generation effects — base Souls exhaust quickly
Exhaust payoff cards are needed to capitalize on Soul exhaust
Can deck out (run out of cards) in very long fights if not careful
Requires specific cards to generate Souls mid-combat

act1.card_priorities: Doom application > Direct damage > Block cards > Soul generation
act1.elite_readiness: Osty gives the Necrobinder a natural advantage in early fights — use it. Osty tanking + your damage should handle Act 1 elites.
act1.boss_preparation: Ensure you have enough combined damage (direct + Doom) to handle the boss. Osty will likely die in a boss fight — have personal block ready.

Add scaling effects that compound over the act

act2.elite_readiness: Your strategy should be coming together. Use potions to cover gaps.
act2.boss_preparation: Ensure your Doom + damage combo can handle high HP bosses within a reasonable number of turns.

Upgrade key Doom and Osty cards at campfires
Prepare for the specific Act 3 boss

act3.focus: Optimization. Upgrade your highest-impact cards. Ensure consistency.

unique_tips.osty_as_resource: Think of Osty as a secondary HP pool. Enemies hitting Osty for 15 damage is 15 HP you didn't lose. This makes the Necrobinder effectively have more HP than other characters.
unique_tips.doom_math: Always calculate Doom efficiency. If an enemy has 40 HP and you apply 15 Doom, you only need to deal 26 damage (not 40). That's a 35% damage reduction. Doom is most efficient on moderate-HP enemies.
unique_tips.souls_immediately: There is almost never a reason to hold Souls in hand. Play them immediately for free draw 2. The only exception is if you have a specific card that triggers on discard and you want to discard the Soul instead.
unique_tips.osty_resummon_timing: Don't resummon Osty if it would die immediately. Wait until enemies are about to attack (check intent) and resummon so Osty absorbs an attack.
unique_tips.doom_vs_direct_damage: For enemies with less than 30 HP, direct damage is often more efficient than Doom application. Save Doom for enemies with 40+ HP where the threshold check saves significant effort.
unique_tips.soul_exhaust_synergy: Every Soul that exhausts is a free exhaust trigger. If you have exhaust payoff cards (gain block on exhaust, draw on exhaust), Souls become even more powerful.

common_pitfalls.ignoring_osty: Osty is not optional flavor — it's a core strategic resource. Players who ignore Osty management lose a significant defensive advantage.
common_pitfalls.doom_without_damage: Doom alone doesn't kill enemies. You need to deal enough direct damage to push their HP below the Doom threshold. Don't stack Doom without also dealing damage.
common_pitfalls.hoarding_souls: Play Souls immediately. Holding them in hand wastes their free draw benefit and clutters your hand.
common_pitfalls.osty_over_investment: Don't invest so heavily in Osty that your personal cards are weak. If Osty dies in a boss fight (likely), your personal deck needs to finish the job.
common_pitfalls.forgetting_doom_timing: Doom checks at the END of the enemy's turn, not the start. This means the enemy gets one more action before Doom kills them. Plan accordingly.
common_pitfalls.neglecting_personal_block: Osty can't tank every attack. Some enemies always target you directly. Maintain personal block density.
